svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.30.3.2 Strip Direction and End Joints
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.30.3.2 Strip Direction and End Joints
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.30 FLOORING

g.text: Plans, schematic. Left of each: the lumber
Plan, supports at 400 mm o.c. as an example. One strip that bears on 2 or more supports outlined red
End joints staggered and over supports, (2)

svg.text: Wood strip flooring is not laid parallel to
lumber subflooring unless a separate underlay
If wood strip flooring is applied without a
subfloor, it is laid at right angles to the
joists so that the end joints are staggered
and occur over supports or are end matched.
If the flooring is end matched, it is laid so
that no 2 adjoining strips break joints in the
same space between supports and each strip
bears on no fewer than 2 supports.
Plans and strip layouts are schematic, support spacing is an example. A shows lumber subflooring on the left.
